topics.label: Lecture introduction and objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class to the final lecture of the course and outlines the session's core learning outcomes.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional treatment modalities—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with their systemic toxicities and efflux-mediated resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss strategies that target distinct cancer cell weaknesses, such as hormone dependence, disrupted cell cycle checkpoints, and defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Oncogenic kinase inhibitors and resistance pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on designing small-molecule inhibitors against hyperactive driver kinases and analyze the biological mechanisms that drive acquired drug resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how therapeutic antibodies can target surface antigens directly to trigger immune effector functions or selectively deliver cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore natural antitumor immune responses and therapeutic approaches to enhance immunity, including checkpoint inhibition, bispecific T-cell engagers, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Current challenges, clinical progress, and future directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize the overarching challenges of tumor heterogeneity, historical treatment outcomes, future therapeutic horizons, and clinical dilemmas.
